chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not upon the slave girl to wear the scarf during the Prayer, nor upon the slave girl assigned to be free upon the death of her master, nor upon the contracted slave girl when it is stipulated upon her to wear the scarf during the Prayer, and she is an owned slave until she pays off the entirety of her contract, and there shall flow upon her whatever flows upon the owned slaves from the legal punishments (Hadd), all of them.'

key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: Legal punishments prescribed in Islamic law
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرَةِ: A slave girl whose master has declared she will be freed upon his death
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبَةِ: A slave girl who has contracted to pay a sum for her freedom

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slave girls wearing the scarf during prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific fiqh of female slaves (ama', mudabbarah, mukatabah) regarding the obligation of the headscarf (qina') during prayer, establishing their exemption while in servitude even if contractually stipulated. It highlights the principle that their legal status regarding hudud and ritual obligations remains tied to their enslaved condition until full emancipation, reflecting the nuanced interplay between ownership rights and religious duty in Shia jurisprudence. The ruling underscores that the master's claim to their labor and status does not automatically extend to imposing additional ritual burdens like the scarf during worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: ‘It is not upon the slave girl to wear the scarf during the Prayer, nor upon the slave girl assigned to be free upon the death of her master, nor upon the contracted slave girl when it is stipulated when the scarf is stipulated upon her, and she is an owned slave until she pays off the entirety of her contract, and there shall flow upon her whatever flows upon the owned slaves from the legal punishments (Hadd), all of them’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once heard abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘A slave-girl is not required to wear a veil for Salat (prayer) as well as one who has planned for her freedom; and the one who has already contracted even if wearing veil for Salat (prayer) is made a condition when she is owned until she pays off all that is contracted and all things applicable to slaves in penal law apply to her also.’”
